items_missed: No agenda statement at all — opened with 'how can I help?' and went straight into discovery. Never laid out the roadmap, never gave a 10-15 minute timeframe, never asked 'sound good?'
Never got the customer's name until the booking step ~8 minutes in, and never asked 'how are you today?'
Never stated the hourly rate. He gave only bundled totals ($550 / $646), then later referenced 'the same hourly rate that we discussed' — a rate that was never actually discussed.

Stairs vs. elevator never resolved. He asked at both addresses ('third floor... with stairs or with an elevator', 'fourth floor... with stairs or elevator') and both times the customer's answer was unintelligible ('Yeah, what's this?' / 'Yeah, both are still a bit'). He said 'Okay, gotcha' and moved on, then built the estimate around 'the hardest part about this move really is just gonna be the stairs' — an assumption, not a confirmed fact.
No Worries Damage Coverage ($2,000) never mentioned
On-Time Guarantee never mentioned — he told her the movers call around 8:00 AM with an ETA but never framed the guarantee or the discount-on-miss
No 'no hidden fees' pitch (no credit card fees, no transportation fees, no fuel surcharge, no assembly fees). He only said individual items 'are not additional charges' as they came up.
Never said how many movers or trucks would be on the job — notable on a job priced per mover per hour, and on a 3rd-floor-to-4th-floor stair carry

Zero Save Your Ass content. No prep-equals-shorter-move framing, no consolidation examples, no 'take a carload' tip — despite the customer literally saying she only had 'a few things left,' i.e. she was already carloading, and despite her asking directly how to reduce the bill.
Quoted before collecting the destination address, then had to retro-attach a $70 trip fee mid-booking ('you actually do have a trip fee... but that was already included in the numbers')
Walk distance and parking never asked at either apartment complex
No additional-stops question, no special-considerations question (long walks, narrow hallways, tight turns), no moving-stressors question
Email confirmation was mentioned only as an afterthought — 'I just don't remember addressing that with you... I forgot if I mentioned it or not'
No BOLDED-details framing for the confirmation email and no 'reply with any corrections' verification ask
No 'any other questions before I let you go?' close and no business hours given
Customer's name used exactly once, at the very end, and mispronounced ('thank you, Rio')
No insurance explanation at all — neither No Worries nor the 60 cents/lb baseline
top_strength: The budget-conscious handling of the minimum was genuinely excellent and honest. When she asked whether dropping the bed would lower the price, he didn't just say yes to close the sale — he told her straight that 'anything less than the two and a half we would still need to charge for the $550,' then built her a better option: 'we could aim to take the couch, the TV, and the TV stand... we still have time during the two and a half hours for the minimum. If you want us to go ahead and add the bed as well.' That turned a price objection into more value for the same money. He also handled the TV question well, explaining the standard TV bag and the blanket/stretch-wrap fallback and that neither is an extra charge, and he was patient and apologetic through a long, painful email-spelling exchange.
coaching_note: Alex, the single highest-leverage fix is that you never said the hourly rate. You quoted $550 and $646 as finished totals and later referred back to 'the same hourly rate that we discussed' — you never discussed one. Lead with it: 'Pricing is super simple — it's [X] per mover per hour, and that covers the truck, gas, taxes, insurance, blankets, wrap, bands and tools. There's a two and a half hour minimum, then we prorate to the nearest fifteen minutes. Does that make sense?' Rate first, then totals, and the totals stop sounding arbitrary. Second priority: you left all three differentiators on the table — No Worries $2,000 coverage, Meet Your Mover, and the On-Time Guarantee. You told her the crew calls at 8:00 with an ETA, which was the perfect open for 'and if we miss that window, we start discounting immediately.' Third, and this one cost her money: when a customer says she has 'a few things left,' that is your Save Your Ass moment, not a reason to skip it — 'anything small that fits in your car, take it the day before, that shortens the move and lowers your bill.' Last thing, and it's a process fix: get both addresses before you quote. You priced the job, then had to walk a $70 trip fee back into a number you'd already given her. Collect addresses in discovery and the quote comes out right the first time.
phone_presence_notes: Patient and genuinely apologetic through a rough email-spelling stretch ('I'm so sorry about that') and honest about the minimum, but transactional overall — the customer's name was used once at the very end, there were no empathy markers or rapport moments, and heavy filler ('yeah, yeah, yeah', 'mm-hmm') carried a lot of the call.
audio_review_reason: Transcript gaps on the customer's side. Her answers to the stairs-vs-elevator questions at both addresses came through unintelligible, so it can't be determined from text alone whether Alex heard a clear answer and moved on appropriately or genuinely let a key estimate variable go unconfirmed.
